answer: Each agent must stake a scarce token before it can submit a trade, and the protocol slashes that stake when an independently verifiable delivery fails. A walnut seller can prove delivery with a signed receipt whose cipher links the order to the agent’s committed identity, while a terrace buyer can challenge mismatches during a fixed dispute window. Creating many fake agents then requires locking more capital and exposes each stake to loss, so identities are costly rather than free.
